title: Residency enforcement: candidate metrics + alert thresholds (beta/canary)
content:
Sheet notes (SRE working doc)

Purpose
- Provide initial alerting thresholds for the Hosted data residency enforcement rollout.
- Focus on: (1) customer-impacting denials, (2) enforcement correctness regressions (fail-open/skip), (3) control-plane dependencies (policy evaluator), (4) routing interactions.
- These thresholds are intentionally conservative during canary/beta to avoid paging on expected customer misconfiguration.

Scope / assumptions
- Scope: Hosted + Dedicated enforcement paths (gateway admission + router constraints + downstream write checks). Private/VPC uses customer-managed boundaries; we only track control-plane config actions + any surfaced violations.
- Canary cohorts will include a mix of internal + a handful of pilot enterprise orgs pinned to EU (eu-west) and US (us-east).
- During beta, we expect non-zero violation denials due to:
  - Customers hitting a non-matching base URL/SDK region hint
  - Latched configs / stale policy caches during rollout
  - Previously tolerated cross-region fallback now being blocked

Definitions / metric conventions (expected)
- Many metrics should include labels: org_tier, product_surface (hosted|dedicated), enforcement_point (gateway|router|storage), pinned_region, request_region, decision (allow|deny), deny_reason.
- Where possible, keep cardinality under control:
  - Avoid raw org_id labels on high-volume counters; use sampled tracing tags for per-tenant debug.
  - Provide separate low-volume audit events for per-tenant evidence.

-------------------------------
TAB 1 — Candidate metrics + proposed alert thresholds

Columns:
A Metric
B Example query (PromQL-ish; refine with actual naming)
C Baseline expectation (canary/beta)
D Warning threshold (canary/beta)
E Critical threshold (canary/beta)
F GA target threshold (steady-state)
G Window
H Paging / routing
I Notes

1) Customer-impacting: denial rate
A: residency_enforcement_decisions_total{decision="deny",enforcement_point="gateway"}
B: sum(rate(residency_enforcement_decisions_total{decision="deny",enforcement_point="gateway"}[5m])) / sum(rate(residency_enforcement_decisions_total{enforcement_point="gateway"}[5m]))
C: Canary: 0.1%–1% (expected misconfig). Beta: 0.05%–0.5%.
D: Warn if > 2% for 10m (canary/beta)
E: Crit if > 5% for 10m OR > 2% for 30m (canary/beta)
F: GA: warn > 0.2% for 15m; crit > 0.5% for 15m
G: 10m / 30m
H: Warn → #eng-sre + #eng-platform. Crit → page SRE on-call.
I: Denial rate alone is not sufficient: segment by deny_reason + pinned_region. A spike during rollout may be customer config; SRE should check top orgs via audit events before paging outside-hours.

2) Denials by reason: region mismatch
A: residency_enforcement_decisions_total{decision="deny",deny_reason="REGION_MISMATCH"}
B: topk(5, sum by (pinned_region,request_region) (rate(residency_enforcement_decisions_total{decision="deny",deny_reason="REGION_MISMATCH"}[10m])))
C: Canary: should dominate deny reasons; expected.
D: Warn if absolute denies > 5 rps sustained 10m (global) (canary/beta)
E: Crit if absolute denies > 20 rps sustained 10m (global) (canary/beta)
F: GA: warn > 2 rps 15m; crit > 10 rps 15m (global)
G: 10m
H: Warn → Slack only. Crit → page if tied to a single region endpoint and correlated with policy/routing failures.
I: We do not want to page solely on REGION_MISMATCH at low volume; this is often customer misconfiguration. Use as an investigative breakout under “Denial rate”.

3) Denials by reason: fallback blocked / capacity
A: residency_enforcement_decisions_total{decision="deny",deny_reason="FALLBACK_DISALLOWED"}
B: sum(rate(residency_enforcement_decisions_total{decision="deny",deny_reason="FALLBACK_DISALLOWED"}[5m]))
C: Canary/beta: should be near-zero in healthy capacity; any sustained value suggests routing/capacity events.
D: Warn if > 0.2 rps for 10m
E: Crit if > 1 rps for 10m OR > 0.5 rps for 30m
F: GA: warn if > 0.05 rps for 15m; crit if > 0.2 rps for 15m
G: 10m / 30m
H: Crit → page SRE + notify routing on-call (or #eng-routing).
I: This is the most “platform-fault-ish” denial reason; it implies we would have previously failed over cross-region but are now correctly blocked. Needs immediate capacity/routing attention and likely comms to impacted enterprise tenants.

4) Correctness regression: enforcement skipped (fail-open)
A: residency_enforcement_skipped_total
B: sum(rate(residency_enforcement_skipped_total[5m]))
C: Canary/beta: should be 0. Any non-zero indicates fail-open path or missing policy context.
D: Warn if > 0 for 5m
E: Crit if > 0 for 10m
F: GA: same (page on any sustained non-zero)
G: 5m / 10m
H: Warn → immediate triage in #eng-platform. Crit → page SRE + Security Eng (Marcus).
I: This is a compliance risk: “skipped” must be treated as a potential incident depending on impacted scope. If intended fail-open exists for specific internal tenants, it must be explicitly labeled and excluded.

5) Policy evaluator dependency: fetch error rate
A: policy_evaluator_requests_total{status="error"}
B: sum(rate(policy_evaluator_requests_total{status="error"}[5m])) / sum(rate(policy_evaluator_requests_total[5m]))
C: Canary/beta: < 0.1% steady.
D: Warn if > 0.5% for 10m
E: Crit if > 2% for 10m
F: GA: warn > 0.2% 15m; crit > 1% 15m
G: 10m / 15m
H: Crit → page SRE + control plane lead (Ethan).
I: Correlate with residency_enforcement_skipped_total and gateway 5xx. If evaluator outages force deny-all, customer impact will be immediate.

6) Policy evaluator latency
A: policy_evaluator_request_duration_seconds_bucket
B: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(policy_evaluator_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
C: Canary/beta: p99 < 50ms (in-region), < 100ms worst.
D: Warn p99 > 150ms for 10m
E: Crit p99 > 300ms for 10m
F: GA: warn > 100ms 15m; crit > 200ms 15m
G: 10m / 15m
H: Warn → Slack. Crit → page if correlated with gateway latency / admission timeouts.
I: Residency checks run on the request path; latency regressions can cause widespread SLO impact even if decisions are correct.

7) Gateway enforcement health: middleware error / exception
A: residency_gateway_middleware_errors_total
B: sum(rate(residency_gateway_middleware_errors_total[5m]))
C: Canary/beta: 0.
D: Warn if > 0.01 rps for 10m
E: Crit if > 0.1 rps for 10m
F: GA: warn > 0.005 rps 15m; crit > 0.05 rps 15m
G: 10m / 15m
H: Crit → page SRE + gateway owner (Amara).
I: This captures code regressions, config parsing errors, etc. Pair with 5xx rate at gateway.

8) Router constraint violations (attempted cross-region route while pinned)
A: residency_router_constraint_violations_total
B: sum(rate(residency_router_constraint_violations_total[5m]))
C: Canary/beta: should be ~0; any sustained value implies routing is still attempting forbidden fallback.
D: Warn if > 0 for 10m
E: Crit if > 0 for 30m
F: GA: same
G: 10m / 30m
H: Warn → routing channel. Crit → page routing on-call + SRE.
I: Distinct from customer-deny; this indicates internal policy/routing mismatch (bug or misconfigured routing tables).

9) Downstream write enforcement: blocked writes
A: residency_storage_write_denied_total
B: sum(rate(residency_storage_write_denied_total[10m]))
C: Canary/beta: should be 0 (assuming admission works). Non-zero indicates we admitted request but later attempted a cross-region write.
D: Warn if > 0 for 10m
E: Crit if > 0 for 30m
F: GA: same
G: 10m / 30m
H: Crit → page SRE + data plane lead (Vikram) + Security.
I: This is both correctness + possible data-handling risk. Even if “denied” prevented persistence, it indicates a pipeline mis-route.

10) Audit pipeline health: residency audit events missing / exporter lag
A: audit_exporter_queue_lag_seconds (or exporter_delivery_latency)
B: max_over_time(audit_exporter_queue_lag_seconds[15m])
C: Canary/beta: < 60s typical.
D: Warn > 300s for 15m
E: Crit > 900s for 15m
F: GA: warn > 180s; crit > 600s
G: 15m
H: Crit → page SRE; notify GRC (Olga) if prolonged.
I: Audit evidence is part of the product promise; missing events will create security review escalations even if enforcement works.

11) Customer-facing: error code rate (RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH)
A: api_errors_total{error_code="RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH"}
B: sum(rate(api_errors_total{error_code="RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH"}[5m]))
C: Canary/beta: moderate; depends on cohort.
D: Warn > 10 rps for 10m (global)
E: Crit > 50 rps for 10m (global)
F: GA: warn > 5 rps; crit > 20 rps
G: 10m
H: Slack only unless paired with gateway 5xx / evaluator failures.
I: This is mostly a proxy for customer experience and documentation gaps. Use to prioritize outbound comms and SDK guidance.

12) Enforcement decision “unknown” / unexpected deny_reason
A: residency_enforcement_decisions_total{deny_reason="UNKNOWN"}
B: sum(rate(residency_enforcement_decisions_total{decision="deny",deny_reason="UNKNOWN"}[10m]))
C: Canary/beta: 0.
D: Warn if > 0 for 10m
E: Crit if > 0 for 30m
F: GA: same
G: 10m / 30m
H: Crit → page SRE + platform.
I: Treat as a bug until proven otherwise; unknown reasons hinder supportability and may indicate policy parsing issues.

-------------------------------
TAB 2 — Expected baseline violation rates (beta/canary)

Goal: set expectations so we don’t over-page early.

Cohort assumptions (rough)
- Canary internal + 3–8 pilot enterprise orgs with pinned_region.
- Request volume in canary is uneven; one pilot can dominate global rates.

Baseline expectations by scenario (order-of-magnitude)
- Correctly configured clients (correct base URL/region hint):
  - Deny rate: ~0%
  - REGION_MISMATCH errors: ~0 rps
- Misconfigured clients (wrong endpoint / stale region hint):
  - Deny rate: 50–100% for that tenant until fixed
  - Global deny rate depends on volume share; can appear as 0.5–5% globally during early beta
- Capacity event in a pinned region (without override):
  - FALLBACK_DISALLOWED denies can spike quickly (0.1–5 rps global depending on scale)
  - Strong signal; likely page-worthy if sustained >10m
- Policy evaluator partial outage:
  - Either deny-all or skip depending on configured fail behavior
  - Both are page-worthy, but for different reasons:
    - deny-all => immediate customer impact
    - skip => compliance risk

Beta-specific tuning guidance
- For canary/beta: prioritize paging on internal regressions (skipped enforcement, router constraint violations, storage write denies, evaluator errors) over customer misconfig.
- Always have a “Top tenants causing denials” debug view available via audit logs/tracing sampling, not via high-cardinality metrics.

-------------------------------
TAB 3 — Proposed alert routing + runbook pointers

Alert name → destination
- ResidencyEnforcementSkipped (any sustained non-zero) → page SRE + notify Security Eng (Marcus) + open incident if scope unclear
- ResidencyStorageWriteDenied (any sustained non-zero) → page SRE + data plane (Vikram) + Security
- PolicyEvaluatorErrorRateHigh → page SRE + control plane (Ethan)
- RouterConstraintViolations → page routing on-call + SRE
- ResidencyDenialRateHigh → page SRE only when paired with FALLBACK_DISALLOWED or correlated platform failures; otherwise Slack + support enablement

Runbook references
- Runbook: “residency violation spike” (Confluence) — triage checklist should include:
  1) Segment denies by deny_reason
  2) Check policy evaluator error rate + p99 latency
  3) Check router constraint violations
  4) Check top endpoint regions involved (pinned vs request)
  5) Pull sampled traces for a representative tenant (no raw org_id metrics)
  6) If customer misconfig: provide remediation (correct base URL / SDK region)

-------------------------------
Open questions / TODOs
- Confirm final metric names + label sets from observability PR(s) (redwood/pr_18473) and dashboard pack (observability-pack/pr_417).
- Decide whether any enterprise tenants will have an approved exception allowing cross-region fallback; if yes:
  - ensure exception path is separately labeled and does not trip “constraint violations”
  - add a dedicated metric: residency_cross_region_override_total{reason,approved_by}
- Confirm policy evaluator fail behavior at gateway (fail-closed vs fail-open) and ensure alerts reflect the chosen posture.
- Add “noisy during rollout” suppression policy:
  - e.g., suppress REGION_MISMATCH-only alerts for first 48h of a tenant enablement; still record audit evidence.

Changelog
- 2025-01-22: initial draft thresholds.
- 2025-02-03: added storage write denies + audit exporter lag; adjusted denial rate thresholds to reduce paging during beta.
- 2025-02-07: clarified paging guidance for FALLBACK_DISALLOWED vs REGION_MISMATCH.
